q2_gaps: proverb / clause-level figurative predication — the idiom coherence test is written for fusing a fixed multi-word phrase into one symbol, and says nothing about a whole clause whose literal reading is incoherent ("clothes make people")
notes: Both clauses are bare kind-denoting NPs on each side, so the opaque kind-level relational-generic form at 0.9/0.9 is the prescribed encoding, and the lemmas (person, rag, louse; clothes has no singular) are right. Emitting no connective atom for the bare comma juxtaposition is also correct.
